mainTopic: How ה׳ judges the in-between people, ordinary sinners, and the worst sinners, and how His kindness tips the scale
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about how people are judged. בית שמאי say the in-between people go down to גיהנם, cry out, and come back up. בית הלל say ה׳, who is 'abundant in kindness,' tips the scale toward kindness and saves them. Ordinary sinners are judged for twelve months and become ash, while the worst sinners, such as heretics, informers, and those who led the many to sin, are judged forever. The גמרא then works out how the 'third through fire' fits בית הלל: a half-and-half person who has the bodily sin is refined in the fire, and one without it is saved by kindness. It defines the bodily sinners and the harsh leader who 'casts fear' on the community. It explains how ה׳ tips the scale, adding רבא's limit that a set-aside sin is not erased. רבא teaches that whoever forgives others is forgiven, and the story of רב הונא shows it. The amud ends as רבי אחא בר חנינא starts explaining 'for the remnant of His inheritance,' which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the in-between people cry out and come up, like refined silver
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי finish their view. The בינוניים go down to גיהנם, cry out, and then come up. The proof is זכריה's image of refining the 'third' in fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they cry out and come up, as it says: 'And I will bring the third part through the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested; he will call in My name and I will answer him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of בית שמאי's statement about the in-between people. They suffer in גיהנם, cry out, and are brought back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of a 'third' group put through fire to be refined, not destroyed. בית שמאי read that as the third group of people: neither fully righteous nor fully wicked. Their time in גיהנם cleans them, and when they call out, ה׳ answers.

keyTerms.meaning: they cry out (like a chirping bird), in pain or in prayer
and they come up (out of גיהנם)
the third part, read here as the middle group
and I will refine them, like metal in a furnace

phrases.english: and they cry out and come up,
phrases.notes: This continues בית שמאי's words about the in-between people, who were just described going down to גיהנם.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And I will bring the third part through the fire,
phrases.notes: זכריה 13:9

phrases.english: and I will refine them as silver is refined,
and test them as gold is tested;

phrases.aramaic: הוּא יִקְרָא בִשְׁמִי וַאֲנִי אֶעֱנֶה אוֹתוֹ״,
phrases.english: he will call in My name and I will answer him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes בית שמאי's statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the in-between people go down to גיהנם, are cleaned there, cry out, and come up.

steps.title: חנה's words describe the in-between people
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק supports בית שמאי. חנה said that ה׳ brings down to the grave and brings up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about them חנה said: 'ה׳ kills and brings to life; He brings down to the grave and brings up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another verse that fits בית שמאי's picture. It describes going down and then coming back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'brings down to שאול and brings up' matches this group exactly. They are lowered into גיהנם but not left there. This verse shows the up-and-down journey, while the first verse showed the refining.

keyTerms.meaning: brings down to the grave (the underworld)

phrases.english: And about them Chana said:
'ה׳ kills and brings to life,
He brings down to the grave and brings up.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second verse supporting בית שמאי's view from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the in-between people go down to גיהנם and come back up

steps.title: בית הלל‎: ה׳ tips the scale toward kindness
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree with בית שמאי. Because ה׳ is 'abundant in kindness,' He tips the balance toward kindness, so the in-between people do not go down. דוד's words 'I love that ה׳ hears my voice' refer to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: 'And abundant in kindness' means He tilts toward kindness. And about them דוד said: 'I love that ה׳ hears my voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now we hear the other side. בית הלל say that the in-between people are spared, because ה׳ leans toward kindness when the scale is balanced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that these people have equal merits and sins. בית שמאי say they must be cleaned in גיהנם first. בית הלל read 'ורב חסד' to mean ה׳ tips the even scale to the good side, so they skip גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: and abundant in kindness (one of ה׳'s attributes)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: the in-between people go to גיהנם briefly and come up. בית הלל‎: ה׳ tips the scale toward kindness, and they are saved.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
'And abundant in kindness' —
phrases.notes: שמות 34:6

phrases.english: He tilts toward kindness.
phrases.notes: When someone's merits and sins are exactly even, ה׳ tips the scale to the good side.

phrases.english: And about them David said:
'I love that ה׳ hears my voice,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's view, which disagrees with בית שמאי's view in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ tips the balanced scale toward kindness, so the in-between people are spared.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a basic idea about how ה׳ judges: when the scale is even, His kindness decides the outcome.

steps.title: The whole chapter of 'דלותי ולי יהושיע' refers to them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that the entire chapter in תהלים, including 'I was brought low and He saved me,' was said about the in-between people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about them דוד said the whole chapter: 'I was brought low, and He saved me.'
steps.whatsHappening: More support for בית הלל. The whole chapter of תהלים fits this group, especially the line 'I was poor, yet He saved me.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דלותי' (I was brought low) sounds like 'poor.' These people are poor in מצוות, since their merits are only half the scale, yet ה׳ still saves them.

keyTerms.meaning: the whole passage, the entire chapter
I was brought low, I was poor

phrases.english: And about them David said
the whole entire passage —
'I was brought low, and He saved me.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:6. Think of it as 'poor in מצוות,' yet still saved.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲלֵיהֶם אָמַר דָּוִד כׇּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the proof from step 3 to the whole chapter of תהלים.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ saves the in-between people even though they are lacking in merit

steps.title: Ordinary sinners are judged for twelve months and become ashes
steps.stepSummary: Jewish and non-Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies are judged in גיהנם for twelve months. Afterward their bodies and souls are destroyed and scattered as ash under the feet of the צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jewish sinners with their body and non-Jewish sinners with their body go down to גיהנם and are judged there twelve months. After twelve months their body is consumed, their soul is burned, and a wind scatters them under the soles of the feet of the righteous, as it says: 'And you shall trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on from the in-between people to a new group: real sinners. It explains how long they are punished and what happens to them afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the in-between people, who come back up, this group does not return. After a set limit of twelve months they are destroyed and turned to ash. The verse in מלאכי gives the picture of ashes under the feet of the righteous.

keyTerms.meaning: Jewish sinners who sinned with their body
twelve months, the limit of their judgment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this group up with the in-between people. They also spend time in גיהנם, but they come out alive. This group ends as ash.

phrases.english: Jewish sinners with their body,
and sinners of the nations of the world with their body —
go down to Gehinnom
and are judged there for twelve months.
After twelve months —
their body is consumed and their soul is burned,
and a wind scatters them
under the soles of the feet of the righteous,
as it says: 'And you shall trample the wicked,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי יִהְיוּ אֵפֶר תַּחַת כַּפּוֹת רַגְלֵיכֶם״.
phrases.english: for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet.'
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the in-between people to the next group in the ברייתא, ordinary sinners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sinners who sinned with their body are judged for twelve months, then destroyed and turned to ash.

steps.title: The worst sinners are judged forever
steps.stepSummary: Heretics, informers, אפיקורסים, those who denied the תורה or תחיית המתים, those who separated from the community, those who spread terror, and those who caused the masses to sin, like ירבעם בן נבט, are judged in גיהנם for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the heretics, the informers, and the אפיקורסים who denied the תורה, those who denied תחיית המתים, those who separated from the ways of the community, those who cast terror on the land of the living, and those who sinned and caused the many to sin, such as ירבעם בן נבט and his companions, go down to גיהנם and are judged there for all generations, as it says: 'And they will go out and see the corpses of the people who rebelled against Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אבל' (but) sets up a contrast with the previous group. These sinners do not finish after twelve months. Their judgment never ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What these people have in common is that their sin goes beyond a personal act. They rejected the foundations of belief, betrayed or abandoned the community, or pulled others into sin. For that reason their punishment has no time limit, as the verse in ישעיהו describes.

keyTerms.meaning: informers, people who hand Jews over to the authorities
people who scorn the תורה and its teachers
for generations upon generations, without end

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: in-between people (cleaned, or saved by kindness), ordinary sinners (twelve months, then ash), and the worst sinners, who undermine faith or the community (forever).

phrases.english: But the heretics, the informers, and the apikorsim
who denied the Torah,
and those who denied the resurrection of the dead,
and those who separated from the ways of the community,
and those who spread their terror over the land of the living,
and those who sinned and caused the many to sin,
such as Yerovam ben Nevat and his companions —
go down to Gehinnom
and are judged there for all generations,
as it says: 'And they will go out and see
the corpses of the people who rebelled against Me, etc.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 66:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 5: these sinners are not limited to twelve months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who deny the foundations of faith, betray or abandon the community, or cause the masses to sin are judged in גיהנם forever.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the most severe sins are those that attack the community's faith or lead others astray, not only personal wrongdoing.

steps.title: Their punishment outlasts גיהנם itself
steps.stepSummary: The worst sinners from step 6 keep being punished even after גיהנם comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: גיהנם will come to an end, but they will not come to an end, as the פסוק says: 'And their form shall wear out the grave, from His dwelling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues describing the worst group of sinners from step 6. It says their punishment lasts longer than גיהנם itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said these sinners are judged 'for all generations.' Now the ברייתא adds that even when גיהנם is finished, they are still not finished. The proof is the פסוק: 'their form' wears out the grave.

keyTerms.meaning: comes to an end, is used up

phrases.english: גיהנם comes to an end
but they do not come to an end,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the worst sinners listed in the last step.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'And their form shall wear out the grave'
phrases.notes: תהלים 49:15. Their being outlasts the grave itself.

phrases.english: 'from His dwelling.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's description of the worst sinners from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment of the worst sinners outlasts גיהנם itself.

steps.title: Why they are punished so severely
steps.stepSummary: They are punished so harshly because they attacked the בית המקדש, which the פסוק calls זבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why all this? Because they stretched out their hands against the זבול, as it says 'from His dwelling (זבול).' And זבול means only the בית המקדש, as it says: 'I have surely built You a house of dwelling (זבול).' And about them חנה said: 'ה׳'s enemies will be shattered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why these sinners get such a harsh punishment. It answers that they attacked the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק from step 7 ends with the word זבול. A second פסוק, where שלמה calls the בית המקדש a בית זבול, shows that זבול means the בית המקדש. So the פסוק itself hints at their crime. The ברייתא closes with חנה's words about ה׳'s enemies being shattered.

keyTerms.meaning: a dwelling place; here, the בית המקדש
they stretched out their hands (they attacked)
His enemies, those who fight Him

phrases.english: And why all this?
Because they stretched out their hands against the זבול,
as it is said: 'from His dwelling,'
and 'זבול' means nothing other than the בית המקדש,
as it is said: 'I have surely built You a house of dwelling,'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:13

phrases.english: and about them חנה said:
'ה׳'s enemies will be shattered.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the punishment described in step 7, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their harsh punishment is because they attacked the בית המקדש (זבול).

steps.title: Two אמוראים add comments about these sinners
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבין says their faces will be black like a pot's bottom. רבא says even the finest people of מחוזא will be among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבין said: Their faces will look like the bottom of a pot. And רבא said: And they include the very finest people of מחוזא, and they will be called 'people of גיהנם.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים add their own comments about this group of sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק בר אבין describes how they will look: black and sooty like a pot's bottom. רבא adds a sharp comment about his own city, מחוזא: even the people who look the finest there belong to this group.

keyTerms.meaning: the bottom of a pot (black with soot)
מחוזא, a city in בבל where רבא lived

phrases.english: רבי יצחק בר אבין said:
And their faces look like the bottom of a pot.
phrases.notes: He means black and sooty.

phrases.english: And רבא said:
And they include the very finest of the people of מחוזא,
and they will be called 'people of גיהנם.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין: וּפְנֵיהֶם דּוֹמִין לְשׁוּלֵי קְדֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds אמוראים' comments on the sinners described in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worst sinners will have blackened faces, and even respected-looking people may be among them.

steps.title: Challenge to בית הלל from the 'third through fire' פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית הלל's rule that ה׳ tips the scale toward kindness, then challenges it from a פסוק about bringing a third group through fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: בית הלל say: 'And abundant in kindness' means He tilts toward kindness. But it is written: 'And I will bring the third part through the fire'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to בית הלל's view from step 3 and challenges it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל said in-between people do not go down to גיהנם, because ה׳ tips the scale toward kindness. But a פסוק in זכריה speaks of a 'third' group brought through fire and then refined. That sounds exactly like a middle group that does go through גיהנם for a while.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Master said', quoting an earlier source to discuss it
but isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: The Master said: בית הלל say:
phrases.notes: This goes back to בית הלל's words in the ברייתא from step 3.

phrases.english: 'And abundant in kindness' — He tilts toward kindness,
But isn't it written:
'And I will bring the third part through the fire'!
phrases.notes: זכריה 13:9. A 'third' group going through fire sounds like the in-between people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic description and returns to בית הלל's rule from step 3 to challenge it.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's rule that in-between people are spared from גיהנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק describes a third group brought through fire, which seems to be the in-between people going to גיהנם.

steps.title: The 'third' means פושעי ישראל בגופן
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about fire refers to Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies, not to ordinary in-between people.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about Jews who sinned with their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in זכריה is about a different group: פושעי ישראל בגופן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So בית הלל's rule still stands for in-between people. The 'third through fire' is a separate group, the bodily sinners mentioned in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies

phrases.english: There, it is about Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by moving the פסוק to a different group.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the subject of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'third through fire' are the ordinary in-between people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'third through fire' are פושעי ישראל בגופן.

steps.title: But bodily sinners have no repair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own answer: the ברייתא said bodily sinners are destroyed, so how can the פסוק describe them as being refined?
steps.simpleTranslation: Jews who sinned with their bodies? But you said they have no repair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, bodily sinners are judged for twelve months and then destroyed into ash. But the פסוק in זכריה describes the third group being refined and then calling out to ה׳. That means they get fixed, which does not fit people who have no repair.

phrases.english: Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies?
But didn't you say they have no repair?!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 5: after twelve months they are destroyed and turned to ash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11 using the ruling of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the 'third through fire' are bodily sinners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bodily sinners are destroyed with no repair, but the פסוק's third group is refined and saved.

steps.title: Half sins, half merits, plus the bodily sin
steps.stepSummary: Bodily sinners have no repair only when most of their deeds are sins. The 'third through fire' are people who are exactly half and half, but whose sins include the bodily sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: When do they have no repair? When most of their deeds are sins. Here, it is people who are half sins and half merits, and among their sins is the sin of Jews who sinned with their bodies. They cannot escape 'And I will bring the third part through the fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting bodily sinners into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a bodily sinner has mostly sins, he is destroyed with no repair, as in step 5. But if he is exactly half and half, and one of his sins is the bodily sin, he goes through the fire, is refined, and comes out. Kindness does not tip the scale for him because of that serious sin.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no way around it for him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think every bodily sinner is destroyed. The גמרא now says that only applies when most of his deeds are sins. A half-and-half person with the bodily sin goes through the fire and comes out.

phrases.english: When do they have no repair?
When most of their deeds are sins.
Here, it is people who are half sins and half merits,
and they also have among them
the sin of Jews who sinned with their bodies,
there is no way for them to avoid
'And I will bring the third part through the fire.'
phrases.notes: Literally, 'it doesn't work for him without' this פסוק; he must go through the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי לֵית לְהוּ תַּקָּנָה — בְּרוֹב עֲוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by limiting step 5 to people with mostly sins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case into two kinds of bodily sinners
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All bodily sinners are destroyed with no repair.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only bodily sinners with mostly sins are destroyed. Half-and-half people with the bodily sin go through the fire and are refined.

steps.title: Without the bodily sin, kindness tips the scale
steps.stepSummary: If a half-and-half person does not have the bodily sin, ה׳'s kindness tips the scale and he is saved. About these people דוד said 'I love that ה׳ hears.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But if not, 'and abundant in kindness' means He tilts toward kindness. And about them דוד said: 'I love that ה׳ hears.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer and brings בית הלל's rule back in full force for in-between people without the bodily sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the picture is complete. A half-and-half person with the bodily sin goes through the fire. A half-and-half person without it is saved by ה׳'s kindness, just as בית הלל said in step 3.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three outcomes: mostly sins plus the bodily sin means destruction. Half and half plus the bodily sin means going through the fire and being refined. Half and half without the bodily sin means ה׳'s kindness saves them.

phrases.english: But if not,
phrases.notes: He means: if the half-and-half person does not have the bodily sin.

phrases.english: 'And abundant in kindness' — He tilts toward kindness.
And about them דוד said:
'I love that ה׳ hears.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:1

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָאו, ״וְרַב חֶסֶד״ — מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי חֶסֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 13 and returns to בית הלל's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In-between people without the bodily sin are saved by ה׳'s kindness. Those with the bodily sin pass through the fire and are refined.

steps.title: רבא explains 'I love that ה׳ hears'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the פסוק דוד said about the in-between people: כנסת ישראל feels loved when ה׳ listens to her prayers, and even though she is poor in מצוות, it is fitting for ה׳ to save her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק 'I love that ה׳ hears' mean? כנסת ישראל said to ה׳: 'Master of the world, when do I know You love me? When You hear my prayers.' And the פסוק 'I was brought low and He saved me' means: 'Even though I am poor in מצוות, it is fitting for You to save me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last step quoted the פסוק 'I love that ה׳ hears' about the in-between people. Now רבא explains what that פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the פסוק as the voice of כנסת ישראל‎: ה׳'s love shows when He listens to our prayers. The second פסוק, 'I was brought low,' fits the in-between person well. Even someone low in מצוות can be saved because ה׳ chooses to save him.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or explained a deeper meaning of a פסוק
The Jewish people as one whole
Poor or lacking (here, lacking in מצוות)

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
"I love that ה׳ hears"
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:1. This is the same פסוק the last step used about the in-between people.

phrases.english: The Jewish people said
before the Holy One, blessed be He:
Master of the world,
when am I loved by You?
When You hear the voice of my pleas.
"I was brought low, and He saved me"
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:6. The word דלותי sounds like דלה, poor, and the next line builds on that.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלָּה אֲנִי מִן הַמִּצְוֹת —
phrases.english: even though I am poor in מצוות,
it is fitting to save me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the פסוק quoted at the end of step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s love shows when He hears our prayers, and He saves us even when we are poor in מצוות.

steps.title: Who are the Jewish bodily sinners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the ברייתא means by 'Jewish sinners with their bodies.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'Jewish sinners with their bodies' mentioned in the ברייתא, who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase from the ברייתא, 'Jewish sinners with their bodies,' and asks what it means. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-14 depended on this group, but the ברייתא never said exactly who they are. The גמרא now asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Jewish sinners who sin with their bodies
What is it? Who are they?

phrases.english: The Jewish sinners with their bodies,
who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the aggadic explanation back to defining terms in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of 'Jewish sinners with their bodies'

steps.title: רב: A head that never wore תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב says the Jewish bodily sinner is someone whose head never wore תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is a head that never put on תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question: the 'bodily sinner' is a Jew who never put תפילין on his head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin is called 'with their body' because the מצוה of תפילין is done with the body itself. Someone who never once put on תפילין fails with his own body.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, worn on the head and arm

phrases.english: Rav said: a head
that did not put on tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: קַרְקַפְתָּא דְּלָא מַנַּח תְּפִלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A Jewish bodily sinner is one whose head never wore תפילין.

steps.title: רב: The bodily sinners of the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא also defines the bodily sinners of the nations. רב says it means those who commit 'the sin,' meaning forbidden relationships.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the sinners of the nations who sin with their bodies? רב said: with 'the sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the second group from the ברייתא, non-Jews who sin with their bodies, and רב defines it in one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'who are they?' is not written again, but it is understood from the step before. For the nations, the bodily sin is not about תפילין, which they were never commanded. It is 'the sin,' a sin done with the body.

keyTerms.meaning: The nations of the world, non-Jews
Sin; here 'the sin' means forbidden relationships

phrases.english: The sinners of the nations of the world with their bodies,
phrases.notes: The question 'who are they?' is left out but understood from the line before.

phrases.english: Rav said: with the sin.
phrases.notes: 'The sin' here means forbidden relationships.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question and answer, now about the nations
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bodily sinners of the nations are those who commit forbidden relationships.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The leader who frightens the community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines another group from the ברייתא, 'those who cast their fear over the land of the living.' רב חסדא says it is a community leader who scares the public too much, not for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'those who cast their fear over the land of the living,' who are they? רב חסדא said: This is a community leader who puts too much fear on the public, not for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one more phrase from the ברייתא. רב חסדא says it describes a harsh community leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase comes from the ברייתא's list of people punished forever. רב חסדא makes it specific: a leader who rules by fear for his own power, not for ה׳'s sake. Being strict when it is truly for Heaven's sake is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for the sake of Heaven

phrases.english: And those who cast their fear over the land of the living,
phrases.notes: Another group from the ברייתא's list of people punished forever; the question 'who are they?' is understood.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: This is a community leader
who puts excessive fear on the community
not for the sake of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the groups named in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a leader who puts excessive fear on the public, not for the sake of Heaven.

steps.title: A harsh leader will not have a Torah scholar son
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: a leader who puts excessive fear on the public, not for Heaven's sake, will not have a son who is a תלמיד חכם. He brings a פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Any community leader who puts too much fear on the public, not for the sake of Heaven, will not see a son who is a תלמיד חכם. As the פסוק says: 'Therefore men fear him; he will not see any of the wise of heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: After רב חסדא's definition, the גמרא adds another punishment for this same harsh leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק, 'men fear him,' describes the leader who frightens people. The second half, 'he will not see the wise of heart,' is read as his punishment: no wise, learned son.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's groups are now defined: the Jewish bodily sinner never wore תפילין, the nations' bodily sinner commits forbidden relationships, and 'those who cast fear' are harsh leaders who act not for Heaven's sake.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Any community leader who puts excessive fear
on the community not for the sake of Heaven
will not see a son who is a Torah scholar,
as it says: "Therefore men fear him;
phrases.notes: איוב 37:24

phrases.english: he will not see any of the wise of heart."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further punishment for the same leader defined in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leader who frightens the public not for Heaven's sake will not have a son who is a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: How does ה׳ tip the scale toward kindness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית הלל's rule again, that ה׳ tips the scale toward kindness, and asks how He actually does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: 'Abundant in kindness' means He tips the scale toward kindness. How does He do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back בית הלל's words from earlier, this time to ask a new question: how does the tipping work? This sets up two answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 used this line to start a challenge. Now it is repeated for a new reason: to ask how it works. With exactly half merits and half sins, what does ה׳ do to the scale?

phrases.english: Beis Hillel say:
"and abundant in kindness"
phrases.notes: שמות 34:6, one of ה׳'s thirteen attributes of mercy.

phrases.english: He tilts the scale toward kindness.
How does He do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to בית הלל's rule from the ברייתא (step 3) to ask how it works
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The way ה׳ tips an evenly balanced scale toward kindness

steps.title: רבי אליעזר‎: ה׳ pushes down
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says ה׳ 'presses down' on the scale, based on the פסוק 'He will press down our sins.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: He presses it down, as the פסוק says: 'He will again have mercy on us; He will press down our sins.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the first answer: ה׳ presses on the scale so the good side wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a balanced scale. ה׳ presses down the side of the merits, so it outweighs the sins. רבי אליעזר's word for this, כובשו, comes straight from the פסוק in מיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He will press down (overpower) our sins

steps.confusionAlert: Both answers lead to the same result, the good side wins. They only disagree on how: pushing the merits down (רבי אליעזר) or lifting the sins up (רבי יוסי בר חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He presses it down,
phrases.notes: He means ה׳ presses down the merit side of the scale so it wins.

phrases.english: as it says: "He will again have mercy on us;
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:19

phrases.english: He will press down our sins."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ presses down the merit side so it outweighs the sins.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא: ה׳ lifts up the sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says ה׳ 'lifts' the sins, based on the פסוק 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: He lifts, as the פסוק says: 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא gives a second answer: ה׳ lifts the sin side of the scale, so the merits win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of adding weight to the good side, ה׳ raises the sin side, as if lifting the sins off. The word נושא in the פסוק means both 'carries' and 'forgives.' Either way, the in-between person comes out with merits.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's 'tipping toward kindness' is explained two ways: רבי אליעזר says ה׳ pushes the merits down, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא says He lifts the sins up.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: נוֹשֵׂא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: He lifts,
phrases.notes: He means ה׳ raises the sin side of the scale, making it lighter.

phrases.english: as it says: "He lifts sin
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:18

phrases.english: and passes over transgression."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: נוֹשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ lifts the sin side of the scale so the merits outweigh it.

steps.title: ה׳ sets aside the first sin each time
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that ה׳ sets aside the first sin, and that this is His way of mercy. With one sin removed, a balanced scale tips toward merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sage from the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: ה׳ sets aside each person's first sin, and that is His attribute of mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer to the question in Step 21: how exactly does ה׳ tip the scale toward kindness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said ה׳ presses down on the scale, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא said He lifts the sins. This ברייתא gives a more exact picture: ה׳ sets aside the first sin. When merits and sins are exactly equal, taking away that one sin tips the balance toward merit.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the school of רבי ישמעאל taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The first one, for each and every person: the first sin is set aside
Attribute, here ה׳'s way of mercy

phrases.english: A sage of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
He removes the first, the first [sin],
phrases.notes: For each person, ה׳ sets aside the first sin so it isn't weighed on the scale.

phrases.english: and that is the attribute [of mercy].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of Step 21, alongside רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ tips the scale by setting aside a person's sins one by one, starting with the first.

steps.title: The set-aside sin is not really erased
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the sin ה׳ sets aside is not deleted. If the person ends up with mostly sins, that sin is counted again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The sin itself is not erased. If a person has a majority of sins, the set-aside sin is counted together with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the ברייתא of Step 24: removing the first sin only helps when the scale is balanced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a sin is a tie-breaker, not a full pardon. If the person's sins are the majority anyway, the removed sin goes back into the count, and he is judged for all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is counted together with them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ה׳ forgives the first sin forever. רבא says it only stops counting when the scale is evenly balanced.

phrases.english: Rava said:
But the sin itself is not erased.
For if there is a majority of sins,
it is counted together with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְעָוֹן עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ נִמְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A set-aside sin is not erased. It counts again if the sins are the majority.

steps.title: Whoever forgives others is forgiven
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression' another way: ה׳ lifts the sins of a person who lets go of wrongs done to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whoever lets go of what others owe him, Heaven lets go of all his sins, as it says, 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression.' Whose sin does He lift? The sin of one who passes over a transgression done against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new reading of the פסוק from Step 23. In his reading the פסוק describes the kind of person ה׳ forgives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, 'passes over transgression' described ה׳‎. רבא reads it as describing the person: ה׳ lifts sin for someone who himself passes over wrongs. The reward matches the deed: if you let go, Heaven lets go.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lets go of his reckonings, who does not insist on settling scores

steps.whyThisMatters: This famous teaching ties how Heaven judges a person to how he treats others, and the story that follows builds on it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whoever lets go of his reckonings [with others],
they let go of all his sins for him,
as it is said: "He lifts sin and passes over transgression."
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:18

phrases.english: For whom does He lift sin?
For one who passes over transgression [done against him].
phrases.notes: Here רבא reads the end of the פסוק as describing the person, not ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כׇּל הַמַּעֲבִיר עַל מִדּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the same פסוק from Step 23 in a new way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgives wrongs done to him has all his sins forgiven by Heaven.

steps.title: רב הונא nearly dies and recovers
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע becomes deathly ill. רב פפא expects him to die and tells them to prepare shrouds. רב הונא recovers, and רב פפא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע got sick, and רב פפא came to visit him. He saw that רב הונא was dying and told the people to prepare his shrouds. In the end רב הונא recovered, and רב פפא was embarrassed to face him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will show רבא's teaching from Step 26. This part only sets the scene; the lesson comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone could see that רב הונא was about to die. His surprise recovery raises the question of why he was saved, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask after his health, to visit the sick
Provisions for a journey, here meaning burial shrouds

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲלַשׁ,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua became sick,
and Rav Pappa went in to ask after him.
He saw that the world was growing weak for him,
phrases.notes: In other words, he looked like he was dying.

phrases.english: He said to them: Prepare provisions for him.
phrases.notes: "Provisions" for his last journey, a gentle way of saying burial shrouds.

phrases.english: In the end he recovered,
and Rav Pappa was embarrassed to see him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲלַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will support רבא's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רב הונא was close to death and recovered.

steps.title: רב הונא was saved because he forgave others
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports that he really was about to die, but ה׳ told the heavenly court not to be strict with him because he was never strict with others. This proves רבא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked him: What did you see? He said: Yes, I really was dying. But ה׳ said to the heavenly court: Since he does not insist on his rights, do not be strict with him. As it says, 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression.' Whose sin does He lift? The sin of one who passes over transgression.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the lesson: רב הונא lived because he forgave others, just as רבא taught in Step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא was not wrong about how sick רב הונא was. The verdict was changed in Heaven. ה׳ judged רב הונא the same way רב הונא treated people, which is exactly רבא's reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not stand on his rights, does not insist on what is owed to him
Do not stand strictly against him in judgment

steps.whatToRemember: Heaven judges a person the way he treats others. If he lets go of what people owe him, Heaven lets go of his sins.

phrases.english: They said to him: What did you see?
He said to them: Yes, it was so,
phrases.notes: He means: I really was about to die.

phrases.english: but the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" here means the heavenly court.

phrases.english: Since he does not stand on his rights,
do not stand [strictly] against him,
as it is said: "He lifts sin and passes over transgression,"
For whom does He lift sin?
For one who passes over transgression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and gives its lesson.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's teaching that one who forgives others is forgiven (Step 26).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's report that ה׳ spared him because he did not insist on his rights.

steps.title: A blessing with a thorn: only the remnant
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא points out that the next words of the פסוק, 'for the remnant of His inheritance,' contain something good with something painful: forgiveness is for the remnant, not for all.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the remnant of His inheritance': רבי אחא בר חנינא said: This is like a fat tail with a thorn in it. It says 'for the remnant of His inheritance,' and not for all His inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the same פסוק in מיכה. רבי אחא בר חנינא begins his explanation, and it continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat tail is a choice piece of meat, so it stands for the good news that ה׳ forgives. The thorn is the catch: the פסוק limits this forgiveness to 'the remnant,' meaning only some of the people and not all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: For the remnant of His inheritance
Fat tail of a sheep, a choice piece
And a thorn in it: something painful inside something good

phrases.english: "For the remnant of His inheritance,"
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק in מיכה 7:18.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
A fat tail, with a thorn in it:
"For the remnant of His inheritance"
and not for all His inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לִשְׁאֵרִית נַחֲלָתוֹ״, אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s forgiveness in the פסוק is for the remnant of His inheritance, not for all of it: good news with a sharp edge.
